summary: Dependency resolved from unpinned GitHub repository
details: package.json declares `"libsignal": "github:wanzchil/libsignal-node"`, resolving the dependency from the HEAD of a GitHub repository with no tag, commit SHA, or integrity hash. On `npm install`, npm fetches whatever that repository currently contains and executes any lifecycle scripts it defines, inside the installer's environment. The content at HEAD can be changed at any time by the repository owner, so the bytes executed on the installer are mutable and not verified against the published tarball. The repository is under the same author account as the package, but off-registry sourcing bypasses the registry's integrity and audit surface regardless of ownership. A a static rule also matched network/command tokens (`ping`, `GET`) in lib/Utils/generics.js, but those appear in ordinary utility code paths rather than an install-time exec sink; the install-time-rce exposure comes from the dependency source itself.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
